questions.prompt: You want to measure the current drawn by a small motor circuit with a multimeter. How do you connect the meter?
options: In parallel across the motor, with the dial on current.
In series with the motor, dial on current.
In parallel across the battery, dial on current.
Touch the probes to the motor wires with the dial on ohms.
questions.explanation: Current is the flow through a path, so the meter must be part of that path: in series. In current mode the meter is nearly a short circuit, so it must never be placed across a source.

questions.prompt: An ESP32 (3.3 V) output pin drives an input of an ATmega328P powered at 5 V. The ESP32 guarantees VOH of at least 2.64 V; the ATmega328P needs at least 3.0 V to read high. What is the right conclusion?
options: It is safe, because 2.64 V is above the 1.5 V low threshold.
It is safe, because both chips use CMOS logic and 3.3 V is high enough.
It fails, because the ESP32 can only drive 5 V signals into 5 V chips.
A high is not guaranteed to read as high, so use a level shifter.
questions.explanation: A guaranteed output high of 2.64 V is below the 3.0 V minimum input high at 5 V, so the read can fail with temperature or part variation. Check VOH(min) against VIH(min), not typical values.

questions.prompt: In a datasheet, what does an absolute maximum rating tell you?
options: A stress limit: exceeding it may damage the part.
The value the part will reach on average at 25 degrees Celsius.
The range in which every listed specification is guaranteed.
The value the manufacturer recommends for the best accuracy.
questions.explanation: Absolute maximum ratings are stress limits for survival, not operating ranges. Guarantees come from the recommended operating or test-condition tables; typical values are only typical.

questions.prompt: A 10 k and 20 k divider from 5 V reads 3.33 V with nothing attached. You connect a 47 k input to the output. What happens to the output voltage?
options: It stays 3.33 V, because the divider ratio is fixed by R1 and R2.
It rises, because the load adds current to the output node.
It drops to about 2.9 V, because the load is in parallel with R2.
It drops to 0 V, because any load short-circuits a divider.
questions.explanation: The load is in parallel with R2: 20k || 47k = 14.0k, so Vout = 5 * 14.0 / 24.0 = 2.92 V. The fixed ratio holds only for an unloaded output.

questions.prompt: A red LED (Vf = 2.0 V) runs from 3.3 V at about 5 mA. Give the smallest standard E12 resistor (in ohms) that is at least the calculated value.
questions.explanation: (3.3-2.0)/0.005 = 260 ohm; E12 values are 220 and 270, round up to 270.

questions.prompt: A 12 V battery feeds a 30 k over 10 k divider (output at the middle). Output voltage in volts.
A 24 ohm resistor is connected across 12 V. Power dissipated in watts.
A divider feeding an ADC reads lower than the formula predicts. Explain the likely cause and give two ways to fix it.
rubric: Identifies loading: the ADC or connected circuit is in parallel with R2, lowering the effective bottom resistance.
Computes or states the effect with the parallel formula (for example R2 || RL) rather than only naming it.
Gives two fixes: lower resistor values (stiffer divider, more current), a buffer or op-amp, or choosing a load at least ten times R2.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
